children.text: kāntas te puruṣottamaḥ phaṇipatiḥ śayyāsanaṃ vāhanaṃ vedātmā vihageśvaro yavanikā māyā jaganmohinī |
children.translated_text: Your beloved is <s>Puruṣottama</s> (the Supreme Person); <s>Phaṇipati</s> (the Lord of Serpents) is your couch, seat, and vehicle; the lord of birds, whose essence is the <s>Vedas</s>, (<s>Garuḍa</s>) is your curtain; <s>Māyā</s> (illusion), the enchantress of the world, (is your attendant);

children.text: brahmādisuravrajaḥ sadayitas tvaddāsadāsīgaṇaḥ śrīr ity eva ca nāma te bhagavati ! brūmaḥ kathaṃ tvāṃ vayam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> and the hosts of <s>devas</s> (gods) are your affectionate servants, a retinue of male and female attendants; and your name is <s>Śrī</s> itself — O Blessed Goddess, how then shall we describe you?

children.text: kāntas te puruṣottamaḥ phaṇi-patiḥ śayyā-āsanaṃ vāhanaṃ veda-ātmā vihaga-īśvaro yavanikā māyā jagan-mohinī |
brahma-ādi-sura-vrajaḥ sadayitas tvad-dāsa-dāsī-gaṇaḥ śrīr ity eva ca nāma te bhagavati ! brūmaḥ kathaṃ tvāṃ vayam ||
yasyās te mahimānam ātmana iva tvadvallabho 'pi prabhur nālaṃ mātum iyattayā niravadhiṃ nityānukūlaṃ svataḥ |
children.translated_text: Even your beloved Lord, though capable, cannot fully measure your greatness — which is, like His own, boundless and eternally favorable by nature —

children.text: tām tvāṃ dāsa iti, prapanna iti ca stoṣyāmy ahaṃ nirbhayo lokaikeśvari lokanāthadayite dānte dayāṃ te vidan ||
children.translated_text: yet I, fearless, shall praise you as "servant" and as "one who has surrendered," knowing your compassion, O sole sovereign of the worlds, O beloved of the Lord of the World, O gentle one!

children.text: yasyās te mahimānam ātmana iva tvad-vallabho 'pi prabhur nālaṃ mātum iyattayā niravadhiṃ nitya-anukūlaṃ svataḥ |
tām tvāṃ dāsa iti, prapanna iti ca stoṣyāmy ahaṃ nirbhayo loka-eka-īśvari loka-nātha-dayite dānte dayāṃ te vidan ||
śreyo tvatkaruṇānirīkṣaṇasudhāsandhukṣaṇād rakṣyate naṣṭaṃ prāk tadalābhas tribhuvanaṃ saṃpraty anantodayam |
children.translated_text: The highest good is protected by the kindling of the nectar of your compassionate glance; the three worlds, formerly lost through its absence, now have infinite prosperity.

children.text: śreyo na hy aravindalocanamanaḥkāntāprasādād ṛte saṃsṛtyakṣaravaiṣṇavādhvasu nṛṇāṃ saṃbhāvyate karhicit ||
children.translated_text: For the highest good is never possible for mortals on the paths of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration), the imperishable, or <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> (devotion), without the grace of her who is dear to the heart of the Lotus-Eyed One.

children.text: śreyo tvat-karuṇā-nirīkṣaṇa-sudhā-sandhukṣaṇād rakṣyate naṣṭaṃ prāk tad-alābhas tri-bhuvanaṃ saṃpraty ananta-udayam |
śreyo na hy aravinda-locana-manaḥ-kāntā-prasādād ṛte saṃsṛtya-kṣara-vaiṣṇava-adhvasu nṛṇāṃ saṃbhāvyate karhicit ||
śāntānantamahāvibhūti paraṃ yad brahma rūpaṃ harer mūrtaṃ brahma tato 'pi tat priyataraṃ rūpaṃ yad atyadbhutam |
children.translated_text: That which is the supreme form of <s>Hari</s> — the peaceful, infinite, greatly glorious <s>Brahman</s> — and that embodied <s>Brahman</s> form which is even dearer than that, most wondrous,

children.text: yāny anyāni yathāsukhaṃ viharato rūpāṇi sarvāṇi tāny āhuḥ svair anurūparūpavibhavair gāḍhopagūḍhāni te ||
children.translated_text: and all those other forms of His who sports as He pleases — they say all of these are tightly embraced by you with your own corresponding forms and splendors.

children.text: śānta-ananta-mahā-vibhūti paraṃ yad brahma rūpaṃ harer mūrtaṃ brahma tato 'pi tat priyataraṃ rūpaṃ yad atyadbhutam |
yāny anyāni yathā-sukhaṃ viharato rūpāṇi sarvāṇi tāny āhuḥ svair anurūpa-rūpa-vibhavair gāḍha-upagūḍhāni te ||
